# OWA Robot Test — Coverage Matrix

The **complete inventory of testable UI units**, each with a stable ID. "Coverage" for
this skill is defined against this file: a run (or a chain of runs) reaches full coverage
when **every in-scope row has been exercised with evidence**. Nothing may be silently
skipped — a row is either exercised (PASS/FAIL), BLOCKED with a stated reason, or
EXCLUDED by the policy table below.

> Derived from [components-path.md](./components-path.md) + a source sweep of `src/`.
> If the app UI changes, update the matrix **and bump `matrixVersion`** (the date below)
> — and check whether the affected [user-workflows.md](./user-workflows.md) recipes
> (each cites matrix rows in its `Verify:` line) need the same update.
> Before a full run, spot-check the matrix against `src/` (new `*Comp.tsx` folders =
> new rows).

Previous: **2026-08-11** (**the file watch moved to the DATA DIR, and a lyric's slides
now refresh on a content change — new XW-08, XW-09, XW-10, PM-127.** Every list used to watch
its own directory (`useDirSourceWatching`, one `fs.watch` per mounted `DirSource`); there is now
ONE **recursive** watch on the **data parent dir**, started lazily by `watchDataDir()` the first
time anything registers a `FileSource` listener (`src/helper/dirWatchingHelpers.ts`,
`FileSource.registerEventListener*`). So an edit propagates even to a surface whose list is not
mounted, and a write into a **sidecar** (`<file>.histories`, `-htmls`, `-images`) fires an
`update` for the file it belongs to. **XW-08** is the bug the change fixes: a lyric edited
elsewhere left the **Stage Previewer** panes showing the pre-edit slides — the panes re-rendered
but re-derived from `LyricAppDocumentStageAbstract`'s 3-minute `CacheManager`, and
`getOpenLyricPreviewer()` handed back the cached `openLyric` without re-reading `content`.
`LyricSlidesPreviewerComp` now clears every stage's cache on `update`, so ALL stages refresh, not
just the one that happened to miss the cache. **XW-09** pins the watch itself (data-dir-wide,
lazy, sidecar mapping) and **XW-10** the readdir half — a file added or removed on disk must
reach the list. ⚠️ **XW-10 was measured FAILING 2026-08-11**; both of its causes were fixed in
code and the row is now **re-verified live and PASSING (2026-08-13, run `20260813-2138`)** —
both halves, add and delete, refreshed the Documents list unaided in under 3 s.
**PM-127** is the Stage Previewer header's new **⋮ → Reload**. Denominator 715 → **719**.
Two later corrections, neither re-verified live: watch events are now **debounced 500 ms**
before any filesystem work (a media download writes its file in hundreds of chunks and each one
was costing a stat and a readdir), so allow ~1 s in XW-08/XW-09/XW-10 rather than expecting the
refresh in the same instant; and a failed media download now names its cause in the toast —
see MD-01.)
Previous: **2026-08-10e** (**the media binaries left the app — new MD-05, MD-06.**
`yt-dlp`/`ffmpeg`/`qjs` are no longer bundled (~36 MB out of every installer): they ship as a
separate `bin-<ver>.tar.gz` the user installs from **Settings → Others → Extra Binaries** into
`<data parent>/extra-bin/`. So the MD block gains a **precondition** — on a machine where the
pack is absent, MD-01/MD-02 fail for a reason that is not a bug. **MD-05** covers the panel
(install, version readout, the `Update to <ver>` button, and `Re-extract`, which must work with
no network because the `bin-*.tar.gz` is deliberately kept on disk); **MD-06** covers the guard
that turns a missing pack into a **Media Tools Required** dialog jumping to that panel instead of
a spawn failure — and asserts the cancel path does not double-toast. In dev the download is
mocked from `extra-work/experiment-building/release/`, which `npm i` builds. `extra-bin` is NOT
teardown: leave it installed. Every `bin-helper/…` path in the MD notes is rewritten to
`extra-bin/…`. Denominator 713 → **715**.)

Previous: **2026-08-10c** (**the mismatched-password re-ask no longer throws away what

Previous: **2026-08-10b** (**new ST-34..ST-40 — Export / Import Bible Data.** The XML
bibles of Settings → Bible now have their own bundle, `.owabdata.tar.gz` (`.owabdata.enc`
when protected), picked through the same one-dialog selector + password the data archive
uses and dropped anywhere onto the Bible XML section to import. The rule the rows exist to

## Mandatory core — screen controlling, presenting, locale, and media download (every run)

Three blocks are **never optional**: every run — full-coverage OR focused (e.g. "robot test
bible lookup") — must exercise the **mandatory core** and record its rows in the run
state file.

**1. Screen controlling & presenting** — the app's reason to exist:

> **SP-01, SP-02, SC-01, SC-02, PR-04, KB-05 (or another clear key)** — present at
> least one real content item, verify it on the mini-screen AND on the `screen.html`
> CDP target while showing, exercise the clear controls, then hide/restore.

**2. Locale switch** — the bug class a single-locale run cannot see:

> **LT-01, LT-02** — re-walk the screens the run touched in the OTHER language, assert
> no `Translation for text "…" not found in locale km-KH` console error and no blank
> panel, then restore the starting locale.

`tran()` returns early when the locale is `en-US` (`DEFAULT_LOCALE`) — it never looks a
key up. In Khmer the same call **throws** on a missing key, and with no error boundary
the subtree renders **blank**. So an English-only pass proves nothing about translation
coverage, and typecheck/tests/build all stay green while a screen is broken in Khmer.

**3. Media download (video + audio)** — the one flow that runs external binaries:

> **MD-05, MD-01, MD-02, MD-04** — install the media pack if it is absent, download a
> video AND an audio from the canonical test link (below) through the Background panel,
> then **delete both again**. Nothing else in the app spawns yt-dlp / ffmpeg / qjs, so a
> broken or missing binary is invisible to every other row and to typecheck/tests/build
> alike — and nothing else in the run writes ~100 MB per pass into the user's data dir, so
> the block that creates them owns removing them (MD-04). A run that downloads without
> cleaning up is **incomplete**.
>
> The binaries are no longer inside the app: they are installed from **Settings → Others →
> Extra Binaries** into `<data parent>/extra-bin/` (MD-05), and a download attempted
> without them raises a confirm dialog rather than failing (MD-06). Do NOT delete
> `extra-bin` as part of teardown — unlike the downloaded media, it is not this run's
> garbage, and re-installing it costs ~27 MB every pass.

**Canonical test link** (use this one so runs are comparable):

```
https://youtu.be/ZSsOrph7rJs?list=RDZSsOrph7rJs
```

A report that lacks evidence for any of the three blocks is **incomplete** — say so
explicitly rather than shipping it. Full recipes: test-plan.md §S7 (screen), §S15
(locale) and §S19 (media download).

## Presenting Flow deep mode — a focused run with its own row contract

The argument `presentingFlow` (or `run sheet`) is **not a focus area that trims the run**; it
selects a tracked MODE (SKILL.md §6f, recipe test-plan §S20, model knowledge-base §14)
with coverage accounting ON and this exact scope set:

> **PL-10, PL-29, PL-32..PL-76, PL-81..PL-102 = 69 rows**, every one ending the run with a
> status in `coverage-<runid>.json` (`"focus": "presentingFlow"`).
>
> Plus the **mandatory core** (SP/SC/LT/MD), ridden from the presenting flow itself — present a
> row and drive its `screen.html` target.
>
> Plus, when the run touches them: **PL-77..PL-80** and **NAV-17/18** (the `.owadoc` /
> `.owadata` archives share the presenting flow bundle's code) and **XW-01..07** (a document
> edited in another window must reach the sheet's rows).
>
> **Out of scope in this mode:** PL-01..PL-09, PL-11..PL-28, PL-30/31 — the
> Documents/Lyrics lists and the generic file-list chrome — except where the fixture uses
> them.

The mode's coverage denominator is therefore `68 − EXCLUDED`, reported separately from a
full run's 651. The rows most easily claimed without evidence are called out in the report
template: the **13 screen actions fired against a showing screen** (PL-72/74), the
**folded-sheet walk** (PL-99) and the **performance measurements** (PL-63/70).

## How a run uses this matrix

1. This file is the **static inventory** — never write statuses into it.
2. Track statuses in a per-run state file
   `test-results/robot-test/coverage-<runid>.json` (schema in SKILL.md §"Coverage
   accounting"). Update it after every few rows so an interrupted run can resume.
3. Statuses:
   - **PASS** — interaction performed, expected observable confirmed, evidence recorded.
   - **FAIL** — interaction performed, expectation not met → also file a Finding.
   - **PARTIAL** — some interactions of the row done, others not (say which in `note`).
   - **BLOCKED** — could not exercise; `note` must say why (e.g. "no camera device").
   - **EXCLUDED** — matches a policy exclusion (EX-xx); `note` names the EX id.
4. **Evidence rule:** a row only counts as PASS/FAIL with at least one of: a screenshot
   path, an `evaluate_script` assertion result, or a console/network diff. "I clicked it
   and nothing crashed" without a checked observable = PARTIAL at best.
5. **Coverage formula** (goes in the report):

   ```
   in-scope   = total rows − EXCLUDED
   exercised  = PASS + FAIL
   coverage % = exercised / in-scope × 100
   ```

   Target for a full run: **100% of in-scope rows attempted; ≥ 99% exercised**, with
   every BLOCKED/PARTIAL row listed with its reason. Never inflate the number — an
   honest 97% with reasons beats a fake 100%.

## Policy exclusions (EX)

These are out of scope **by policy**, not laziness. They count separately and never
against coverage. Where a "covered-to-the-edge" trick exists, use it — it converts the
row's control to exercisable while excluding only the un-drivable/destructive tail.

| ID    | Excluded                                                                                                                     | Why                                          | Cover to the edge by…                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| ----- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| EX-01 | OS-native file dialogs (browse/open/save)                                                                                    | Not drivable via CDP                         | click the button, confirm the app doesn't crash while the dialog is cancelled by policy — mark the _dialog itself_ excluded                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| EX-02 | **Leaving** the user's real display taken over, or OS-fullscreen during a live service                                       | The user may be actively presenting (KB §10) | **Showing the screen is now MANDATORY, not excluded** (SP-01/SC-01): toggle it on briefly, drive the `screen.html` CDP target, then hide + restore. EX-02 applies only to _leaving_ it showing, or when the user explicitly said the display is in live use — then assert via mini-screen only and mark the SC rows BLOCKED→EX-02 |
| EX-03 | Camera-dependent rows                                                                                                        | Needs hardware; may be absent                | if a device exists, exercise; else BLOCKED→EX-03                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| EX-04 | Following external links (Help, About links)                                                                                 | Opens the user's browser                     | click-eligibility only: control present, named, enabled                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| EX-05 | Destructive tails: `Clear All Settings`, `Reset All Child Directories`, deleting user documents/lyrics | Destroys user data/state                     | click → **confirm dialog appears → Cancel** (covers the control + dialog); for delete, create a scratch item first, delete _that_. **`Reset Widgets Size` is NOT on this list any more** — it moved to View (NAV-21), only touches pane sizes, and is undone by re-dragging, so that row is taken all the way through **Yes**       |
| EX-06 | App quit / relaunch flows                                                                                                    | Kills the session under test                 | —                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| EX-07 | Downloading new bible versions                                                                                               | Large network payloads on the user's machine | verify list/search/enable-disable UI; toggle an already-downloaded version and restore                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |

| NAV-21 | Native **View → Reset Widgets Size**                                                                                   | **View → Reset Widgets Size** (កំណត់ទំហំ Widgets ឡើងវិញ) → confirm                                          | asks `Are you sure to reset every widget size and reopen the widgets?` with Yes/No. **Yes** sweeps every `widget-size-*` setting (`removeSettingsByPrefix`, so the `-dyn-h`/`-dyn-v`, ad-hoc and per-document keys go too) then restores every mounted pane to its `data-fs-default` **and reopens every collapsed widget**, live. **No** changes nothing. Verify right after a drag — the failure mode is one pane keeping its dragged width. Dev-only entry point `globalThis.tryResetWidgetsSize()` (src: src/resize-actor/widgetAppMenuHelpers.ts, src/resize-actor/ResizeActorComp.tsx) |

## AP — Archive password protection

Optional password protection, shared by all five archive exports. Exercise the rows on at
least one kind per run; the code path is identical for the others (`.owapf` / `.owadoc` /
`.owbible` / `.owabn` / `.owadata`).

| ID    | Unit                              | How to reach it                                                                                    | What to check                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| ----- | --------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| AP-01 | The export password dialog        | right-click any exportable item → **Export**; or `globalThis.tryDataExport()` for the data archive | EVERY export now opens a dialog BEFORE writing anything: **Password** + **Confirm Password** (both `type="password"`), a **Show Password**/**Hide Password** toggle that flips BOTH fields at once, and the hint **Leave empty to export without a password**. The data archive shows the same fields below its folder list, under a separator — ONE dialog, not two (src: src/popup-widget/ArchivePasswordComp.tsx, src/setting/data-archive/dataArchiveMenuHelpers.tsx:59) |
| AP-02 | Empty password ⇒ unchanged export | open the dialog, press **Ok** with both fields empty                                               | writes exactly what the export always wrote — `<name>.owapf.tar.gz` / `.owadoc.tar.gz` / `.owbible.tar.gz` / `.owabn.tar.gz` / `open-worship-data.owadata.tar` — a real gzip/tar that `tar -tzf` still lists. This is the regression that matters most: protection is OPTIONAL and the default path must not change (src: src/helper/archiveNameHelpers.ts `toArchiveDotExtension`)                                                                                          |
| AP-03 | Password ⇒ `.enc` bundle          | type the same password in both fields, **Ok**                                                      | writes `<name>.<kind>.enc` instead. First 7 bytes are `OWAENC\0`, byte 7 is the container version `01`, byte 8 the KDF id `01`, byte 9 `0f` (scrypt log2 N = 15), byte 10 `08` (r), byte 11 `01` (p). `tar` refuses it ("not in gzip format"). No `.part` file is left in Downloads (src: electron/archiveCryptoHelpers.ts)                                                                                                                                                  |
| AP-04 | Mismatched confirmation           | type different values in the two fields                                                            | the dialog says **Passwords do not match** live, and **Ok** re-asks instead of exporting — **inline, with NO intermediate alert popup**, on all five kinds. Press **Ok** a SECOND time without changing anything: it must re-ask AGAIN, still **holding both typed values** and — on the two one-dialog flows (Export Data, Export Bible Data) — **the operator's item selection**. An alert between the two `showAppInput` calls unmounts the popup and blanks both, after which one more Ok exported the whole list UNPROTECTED. Three tries, then the export is abandoned. Also: clearing BOTH fields settles the complaint (empty is the legitimate "no password"), and a value typed into **Confirm Password** alone is flagged rather than silently exported unprotected (src: src/popup-widget/ArchivePasswordComp.tsx `MAX_PASSWORD_ATTEMPTS`, src/setting/data-archive/dataArchiveMenuHelpers.tsx `askForFolders`, src/setting/bible-setting/bibleXMLArchiveMenuHelpers.tsx `askForBibles`; regression tests `tells a NEW listener the values it is already holding`, `tells a NEW listener the selection it is already holding`, `drops the re-ask complaint once both fields are cleared`, `flags a confirmation typed against an empty password`) |
| AP-05 | Import asks for the password      | drag a `.enc` bundle onto its list, or `globalThis.tryDataImport('<path>')`                        | the drop gate ACCEPTS the `.enc` name (it must not fall through to "copy into the folder"), then a one-field dialog says **This archive is password protected**. The right password imports normally — for a presenting flow, under the ORIGINAL archive's base name, never the temp file's (src: src/helper/archivePasswordHelpers.ts `openArchiveForReading`)                                                                                                                     |
| AP-06 | Wrong password, retry, give up    | submit a wrong password                                                                            | rejects in well under a second even on a gigabyte archive (the container's key check answers before any payload is read), re-asks with **Wrong password, try again**, allows three tries in total, then reports failure under the flow's own title. Cancel at the prompt aborts silently with no toast (src: src/helper/archivePasswordHelpers.ts)                                                                                                                           |
| AP-07 | A plain bundle is never prompted  | drag an ordinary `.tar.gz` bundle onto its list                                                    | imports with NO password dialog at all. Detection is by the container magic, not the name — so a plain bundle someone renamed to `.enc` also imports silently, and a `.enc` renamed to something else still asks (src: src/server/appHelpers.ts `checkIsEncryptedFile`)                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| AP-08 | The dialog in Khmer               | switch the app to Khmer, then repeat AP-01 and AP-05                                               | title, both field labels, the reveal toggle, the hint, the mismatch line and the retry line all render in Khmer and the page does NOT blank. `tran()` throws on a missing key in dev, so an English-only pass structurally cannot see a gap here (keys guarded by src/lang/data/km/index.test.ts)                                                                                                                                                                            |

| PL-95  | **Run actions** — `Next: Interval` / `Next: Timeout`                                                                                          | 🖱️R a presenting flow → **Add Action** → **Next: Timeout**, answer **5** (and Cancel the question once); repeat with **Next: Interval** / **3**; 🖱️R each new row; open the floating preview and 🖱️ the timeout element, then let it run out; arm it again and press any key mid-count; arm the interval and click/press keys while it counts, then 🖱️ the ⊗ pill; put an interval directly above a timeout and let it hand over; then 🖱️R a SLIDE row → **Add CC Elements** and read the list; attach the timeout, open the preview and step onto that slide with the next-key; 🖱️R the CC row; then 🖱️R the timeout row → **Change Timing**, switch the chooser to **At Time**, set a time a couple of minutes ahead and 🖱️ the row; repeat with a time that has already gone by; finally CLOSE the preview and 🖱️ a run-action row in the tree | the question is asked BEFORE the entry exists, so **Cancel adds nothing**; the row then reads `⏱ Next: Timeout (5)` / `⟳ Next: Interval (3)` — the number is part of the label in both the tree and the preview's button, and **Change Seconds** (the row's own menu entry, opening on its current value) re-arms it in place. **A TIMEOUT may be armed with a TIME OF DAY instead**: its question's left half is a `Seconds` / `At Time` chooser (the interval's stays a plain `Seconds` label), the time field opens FIVE MINUTES ahead of now when there is no time to open on, the row then reads `⏱ Next: Timeout (7:05 AM)` — 12-hour with AM/PM, from the stored 24-hour `HH:mm`, never the system's own format — and its menu entry says **Change Timing**, re-opening on the half it was armed with. The two are alternatives, never both: re-arming with one DELETES the other. Firing it counts to that time TODAY (the pill reads `m:ss` / `h:mm:ss`, not a five-digit second count), and the remainder is re-read from the wall clock each tick, so a laptop that sleeps mid-count still fires on time. A time that has already gone by is **refused**, with the toast **The set time is already due** titled **Next: Timeout** — it is never rolled over to tomorrow, and nothing is armed. A run action reaches NO screen: its menu is **Start Auto Next** + **Change Seconds** and nothing else — no **Reveal Original**, no **Apply on Screens**, no **Set Specific Screen**, no **Add CC Elements** — it is not draggable onto a mini screen, and it never appears in another row's **Add CC Elements** list. In the preview a warning-coloured pill appears at the widget's top-right showing the seconds left: a TIMEOUT counts down once, forces the next selection at 0 (the cursor moves on, and what it lands on fires exactly as the next-key fires it) and is then spent. **Only the RUN MOVING touches either clock** — the preview's cursor changing to another element or to another slide of the one it is on. That CANCELS a timeout and RESTARTS an interval's count from full; a click on a background, a button, the widget's own chrome, or any keypress that does not move the run, leaves both alone (an unintended click killing the wait was the first design and is a bug). Arming is never cancelled by the gesture that armed it, and tidying the sheet — a reorder that shifts the element the run is on — must not cancel it either. An interval is otherwise ended only by the pill, by closing the widget, or by the end of the sheet. An auto-step that lands on another run action hands the clock over to it. With the preview closed — or open on ANOTHER presenting flow — triggering one toasts **Open the presenting flow preview to use this action** and nothing else happens. **A TIMEOUT may be a CC element and an INTERVAL may not**: the timeout appears in every row's **Add CC Elements** list (its seconds in the label) and the interval never does, so a slide can carry "go on by yourself N seconds later" while nothing can carry a loop no input can stop. A CC'd timeout arms when its HOST reaches a screen — dismiss the "which screen?" menu and no countdown starts — and it raises no second screen question of its own. **Its CC row drops Set Specific Screen for a clock of its OWN**: a hollow `stopwatch` in the action's amber sits where the media controller's gear does, and it (or the row's **Change Timing**) opens the very same question the element's row asks, on whatever this row is counting now. The answer is stored on the ATTACHMENT (`ccItems[].actionArming`), never on the element, so ONE timeout element attached to two lines can hold one for 4s and the other for 30s; the glyph then reads **filled**, and a second entry, **Use Element Timing** (ប្រើការកំណត់ពេលរបស់ធាតុ), appears and hands the row back (glyph hollow again, key deleted). Absence still means the element's, so re-arming the element moves every follower that has none and leaves the overridden ones alone; a time of day written over seconds deletes the seconds, as on the element. A `Jump to`'s pointer never gets the glyph — it is never fired. It moves the run on from where the PREVIEW's cursor is, so a host presented from the tree while the panel sits elsewhere advances the panel, not the tree (src: src/presenting-flow/presentingFlowAutoNextHelpers.ts:1, src/presenting-flow/presentingFlowActionHelpers.ts:190, src/presenting-flow/PresentingFlowPreviewFloatingComp.tsx:106, src/presenting-flow/PresentingFlowCcRowsComp.tsx:140) |

The panel (**Slide: Media Control - Settings**) is asked BEFORE the line exists, so **Cancel adds nothing**; OK writes the action element AND the CC that points at it in ONE go. Fields that mean nothing in the chosen mode are HIDDEN, not greyed: **Pause** drops the start point and the stop point, **Stop** drops only the stop point. **Volume** and **Speed** are behind ticks because "not set" is a real answer — an unticked volume must leave the level the operator set by hand on the mini screen alone. The CC row reads the mode then the numbers (`Slide: Media Control (Play +3s 10s→70s 70% 2x)`, translated mode, numbers appended AFTER it) and carries a cyan **gear** that reopens the panel on its stored values; **Media Control Settings** on its right-click menu is the same door. The listed ELEMENT row shows the bare label with no gear and does nothing when clicked — the settings live on the ATTACHMENT, so the same controller attached to two slides means two different things. Presenting the host then plays EVERY media in that slide: after the delay the video seeks to the start point and runs at the set speed with the set volume, pausing at the media time asked for; the projected screen follows at the SAME speed and stays muted (sound is the presenter machine's, by design), and a canvas `audio` item plays on the presenter only. A **pin narrows** rather than redirects: pinned to a screen the host also reached it runs there alone, pinned to one the host never reached it runs NOWHERE (there is no media on it to drive). **UNSELECTING the host stops what it started**: presenting another slide on that screen — or clearing it — pauses every media of the outgoing slide (native elements and YouTube alike) and drops anything still armed, so the sheet can move on. That is the whole point of it being the SHEET's media: media the operator started by clicking the mini screen still REFUSES the swap with **Media is Playing**, and must be checked both ways — with a controller armed the next slide lands silently, without one the toast still appears and the slide stays. Per-verse color notes need no manifest entry: `ItemBase` keeps them in each item's own `metadata`, inside the file. The bible VERSIONS the verses name are NOT bundled (src: src/bible-list/bibleArchiveHelpers.ts:36, src/bible-list/BibleFileComp.tsx:105) |

A dropped archive is unpacked where it already sits and is never copied into the bibles folder (src: src/bible-list/BibleListComp.tsx:39, src/helper/singleItemArchiveHelpers.ts:236)                                                          |
| PR-29 | Bundle **kind** guard                                                                                                                                            | through **Import**, pick a `.owadoc.tar.gz` in the Bibles list — and a `.owbible.tar.gz` in the Documents list                                         | the manifest's `itemKind` is checked, so each list refuses the other's bundle with `This archive holds a "<kind>", not a <kind>` and writes nothing. (The drop path never gets that far — its suffix gate rejects the other extension first — but the file dialog accepts any `gz/tgz/tar`.) (src: src/helper/singleItemArchiveHelpers.ts:203)                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |

The box stays draggable throughout. **Both the canvas and the slide previews are inside a shadow root, so a CDP hover must pierce it** — dispatch a bubbling `mouseover`/`mouseout` on the `[data-website-item]` element. Hovering a SLIDE THUMBNAIL must NOT go live (only the editor does) |

## XW — Cross-window propagation (multi-renderer edit→present sync)

The class of regression a one-window run misses: OWA windows are **separate renderers**
that sync only via **disk + `fs.watch`**, so an edit in the **separate** `Document Editor`
window must propagate to the Presenter preview / list / live screen. Requires the
**two-window** config (editor opened via NAV-21 external icon → `openPopupWindow`, NOT the
in-place `Slide Editor` tab). Recipe + CDP-drivable-edit techniques (properties numeric
inputs ED-17/ED-19, programmatic `CanvasController`, direct `writeFileData`): KB §12,
test-plan.md §S18. **Prefer a scratch doc; restore via Undo (never Discard).** The chain to
cite when a hop breaks: `writeFileData`→ the ONE recursive `fs.watch` on the **data parent
dir** (`watchDataDir`→`watchDir`→`handleFileEvent`, `src/helper/dirWatchingHelpers.ts`)
→`alertFileChanging`→`FileSource.fireUpdateEvent` on the changed path (**and**, for a sidecar
path, on the file it belongs to)→`useFileSourceEvents(['update'])` consumer reload, through the
2 s data cache — plus, for a consumer with a cache of its own, that cache's own invalidation
(XW-08). Adding or removing a file takes the OTHER half of `handleFileEvent`, the readdir diff
→ `dirSource.fireRefreshEvent()` (XW-10).

> **A disk write is the cheapest XW driver, and the only one that needs no OS focus.**
> Rewriting the file with `node -e` (or writing a `<file>.histories/<n>-head`, which is exactly
> what an editor window does — KB §12.2b) exercises watch→alert→cache→render end to end. Every
> XW row below can be driven that way against a **scratch** file; the editor window is needed
> only when the row is about the editor's own UI.

| ID    | Target                                                                                                                                       | Interactions                                                                                                                                                              | Pass condition                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| ----- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| XW-01 | Editor(separate window) save → **Presenter center preview** (`VarySlidesComp`) (src: src/app-document-presenter/items/VarySlidesComp.tsx:84) | in a scratch doc shown in the Presenter, edit a box via ED-19 numeric inputs (or `writeFileData`) in the editor window → **Save**; observe the Presenter `VarySlidesComp` | within ~3 s the Presenter's center slide preview re-renders with the new geometry/text (500 ms debounce + 2 s cache); a stale preview = FAIL (src: src/app-document-presenter/items/VarySlidesComp.tsx:77-89)                                             |
| XW-02 | Editor save → **Presenter list-row thumbnail** (`VaryAppDocumentFileComp`) (src: src/app-document-list/VaryAppDocumentFileComp.tsx:249)      | same save; observe the Documents left-list row's preview for that doc                                                                                                     | the row's thumbnail reloads to the edited content (the `useFileSourceEvents(['update'])` subscription fires); stale = FAIL — this is exactly the reload path the recent refactor touched (src: src/app-document-list/VaryAppDocumentFileComp.tsx:252-258) |
| XW-03 | Editor save → **live screen output** (`screen.html`) when that slide is presented                                                            | present slide 1 of the scratch doc (SP/SC), then edit+save it in the editor window; screenshot the `screen.html` target                                                   | the presented slide on the real output updates to the edited content; if the mini-screen updates but the screen target does not, that is a screen-only propagation bug (KB §6)                                                                            |
| XW-04 | **Unsaved**-edit semantics (negative check — expected behavior, not a bug)                                                                   | make an edit in the editor window but do **NOT** save; observe the Presenter                                                                                              | the Presenter keeps showing the last **saved-on-disk** version (separate renderers don't share memory) — this is CORRECT; only a _saved_ change that fails to propagate is a FAIL (KB §12.2)                                                              |
| XW-05 | **Reverse** direction — change made/saved from another surface reflects in the open editor                                                   | with the doc open in the editor window, trigger a save/`fireUpdateEvent` from the Presenter side (e.g. a doc/slide op)                                                    | the editor window re-reads and reflects it (its own watcher→bridge→reload); no need to reopen the editor                                                                                                                                                  |
| XW-06 | **Lyric** cross-window edit → lyric render body / list row (`LyricRenderPreviewBodyComp` / `LyricFileComp`) (src: src/lyric-list/LyricFileComp.tsx:80)         | open a lyric in the Lyric Editor popup, edit + save; observe the Documents previewer body and the list row                                                                            | the rendered song and the row reload to the edited content (same `useFileSourceEvents(['update'])` path as XW-02; refactor-touched). The **Stage Previewer** panes under it are **XW-08** — assert them separately: they carry their own cache and used to stay stale while this row passed (src: src/lyric-list/LyricFileComp.tsx:77-85)                                                                               |
| XW-07 | **Data-cache staleness** guard (2 s `fileDataCacheManager`) (src: src/helper/FileSource.ts:42)                                               | after XW-01, if the preview looks stale, wait >2 s and re-trigger (or re-select the doc)                                                                                  | a re-read past the 2 s TTL returns fresh bytes — if the preview is _permanently_ stale even after cache expiry, the reload/subscribe wiring is broken, not the cache (src: src/helper/FileSource.ts:132-149,171-173)                                      |
| XW-08 | **Lyric content change → EVERY Stage Previewer pane** (src: src/lyric-list/LyricSlidesPreviewerComp.tsx:216-225 · src/lyric-list/LyricAppDocumentStageAbstract.ts `clearCache` · src/lyric-list/LyricAppDocument.ts `getOpenLyricPreviewer`) | select a scratch `.owl`, **Add Stage** so ≥2 panes are shown, and read a unique ASCII marker (`ROBOT MARKER ALPHA`) out of each pane's shadow root; change the marker **on disk** — first by rewriting the `.owl`, then by writing `<file>.histories/1-head` (the shape an editor window writes) — and re-read after ~1 s and again after ~5 s | **every** pane shows the new marker within ~3 s — stage 0 and every added stage, plus the lyric render body above them — with **no** click, re-select or Reload, for **both** write shapes (a lyric edited in the Lyric Editor writes only the head until Save). **The two ways this breaks, both silent:** the panes re-render but re-derive from `LyricAppDocumentStageAbstract`'s **3-minute** `CacheManager`, so they serve pre-edit slides for up to 3 min (or for good, if nothing evicts) — the previewer must clear the cache of **each** stage entry on `update`, not just the visible one; and the cached `openLyric` instance the panes derive from must be re-fed `Lyric.getContent()` or it renders the text it was built with. A run that checks only the body ABOVE the stages (XW-06) passes while both are broken. Verified live 2026-08-11: both write shapes, both panes, <1 s. ⚠️ Two later changes, **not re-verified live**: the refresh now runs from `LyricManager.refreshOpenLyricContent()` in the previewer's own `update` handler — **content first, `clearCache()` second**, because a pane re-deriving between the two re-fills the cache from the pre-edit text — and watch events are debounced 500 ms, so allow ~1 s rather than expecting it instantly |
| XW-09 | **The watch is data-dir-wide, lazy, and sidecar-aware** (src: src/helper/dirWatchingHelpers.ts `watchDataDir` / `alertFileChanging` · src/helper/FileSource.ts `registerEventListener*`)                     | with a file's consumer open while its **list is not mounted** (hide the Documents list widget, keep the document previewed), change that file on disk; then write into a sidecar dir — `<file>.histories/<n>-head`, and a `<name>.pptx-htmls` / `-images` entry if one exists — and watch the ORIGINAL file's consumers | ONE recursive `fs.watch` covers the whole **data parent dir**, so propagation no longer depends on which list is mounted (it used to need that dir's own `DirSource` alive via `useDirSourceWatching`), and it is started lazily on the first `FileSource` listener — nothing watches before a window subscribes. A write inside a sidecar fires `update` for BOTH the sidecar path and the file it belongs to (`fileExtraSuffixes` = `.histories` · `-htmls` · `-images`), the original only if it still exists. The suffix test must come FIRST: an ordinary file change may not spend an extra `fsCheckFileExist` on a non-existent "original" |
| XW-10 | **File added / removed on disk → the list refreshes** (the readdir half of `handleFileEvent`) (src: src/helper/dirWatchingHelpers.ts `handleFileEvent`)                                    | with the Documents list open, copy a scratch `.owl` into the documents dir and wait ~5 s; then delete it and wait ~5 s; repeat in a second list (Videos/Images) if time allows                                                                       | the new row appears and the deleted row disappears **without** a manual Reload: `handleFileEvent` diffs the directory listing against `dirSource.filePathsMap` and calls `fireRefreshEvent()` — the only thing that clears that map (the list menu's **Reload** fires `reload`, which does not, so a stale entry survives Reload too). ⚠️ **Measured live 2026-08-11 (refactor28): FAILED**, for TWO reasons, both since fixed in code and **re-verified live PASSING on 2026-08-13** (run `20260813-2138`: a scratch `.owl` copied into the documents dir appeared as a row within 1.5 s, and deleting it plus its `.histories` dir removed the row within 3 s — no manual Reload either way). (1) The watch root is the data PARENT dir, so `handleFileEvent` receives `dirPath` = the parent and `name` = `documents\<file>.owl`; `alertFileChanging` still resolved the right path (which is why XW-08 passed), but the diff called `DirSource.getInstance(dirPath)` — whose argument is a **setting name**, not a path — so it built and cached a junk `DirSource` with `dirPath: ''` and fired `refresh` at nobody. Now resolved through `DirSource.getInstanceByDirPath(pathDirname(filePath))`, i.e. the CHANGED FILE's own directory, skipped when no list is mounted on it. (2) The DELETE half could not have worked either: a path that is neither a file nor a directory returned early, before the reconcile. The existence check is gone from that path — a vanished entry now still reconciles its directory. Note the events are debounced 500 ms, so allow ~1 s before reading the list |

| ST-50 | Deleting a scratch bible leaves its cache behind                                                        | 🖱️ 🗑 on the scratch row → **Yes**; then look at `bibles-data`                     | the confirm is `Delete Bible XML` / `Are you sure to delete bible XML "<key>"?`; **Yes** trashes `<key>.xml` and the row goes — but the sibling **`<key>.xml.cache` folder stays on disk** (13 MB for the canonical file), so a robot run that seeds a scratch bible must remove that folder itself or it accumulates run after run (a stale `ZZTEST.xml.cache` from an earlier run was still sitting there on 2026-08-10) (src: src/setting/bible-setting/bibleXMLHelpers.ts:455-462) |
| ST-51 | `BibleXMLInfoComp` **Reset Bible XML** (KJV row only)                                                    | 🖱️ `bi-arrow-counterclockwise`/`btn-warning` on the **KJV** row → **Yes**        | the button exists on the **KJV row and no other** (it is gated on `bibleKey === BIBLE_KJV_KEY`, so an installed `NIV`/`GKHB` row still shows only ✎ + 🗑). It confirms with `Reset Bible XML` / "Reset this bible XML with the app embedded KJV? All your changes will be lost." (**No**/**Yes**); **Yes** overwrites **the row's own file** — not `<dir>/KJV.xml`, so a KJV kept under another file name is replaced in place rather than duplicated — wipes the sibling `KJV.xml.cache` folder and fires `forceReloadAppWindows()`. An open dirty editor blocks it with the `Unsaved Bible Data` toast, exactly like ST-11/ST-29. **The reset is destructive: it discards the installed KJV, so a robot run must back the file up first** (the dev copy was `English KJV`, the embedded one is `King James Version`) (src: src/setting/bible-setting/BibleXMLInfoComp.tsx:57-90, src/setting/bible-setting/bibleXMLHelpers.ts:459-496, src/helper/bible-helpers/kjvBibleXMLTextHelpers.ts) || ST-52 | **SongSelect Integration** card (`SettingOthersSongSelectComp`, tab `Others`)                           | fill **Client ID** / **Subscription Key** / **Redirect URI** (blur each); 🖱️ **Sign In** (ចូលគណនី) and close the window it opens; 🖱️ the header **SongSelect ↗** | the card sits between the AI-key and Extra Binaries cards with a hint line (`Import song lyrics from CCLI SongSelect`) and fields **Client ID / Client Secret / Subscription Key / Redirect URI**, each saved **on blur** (green `bi-check-circle-fill` appears beside the label; reopening Settings shows the value kept). **Sign In** stays disabled until the three non-secret fields are set (title `Set Client ID, Subscription Key and Redirect URI first`), then opens a REAL browser window on `identityservices.ccli.com/connect/authorize` via the new `main:app:oauth-authorize` IPC (nodeIntegration off, isolated partition); closing that window without completing toasts `Sign in failed` / `Sign in was canceled` (ការចូលគណនីត្រូវបានបោះបង់) and the button returns to **Sign In**. While signed in (a stored refresh token) the row instead shows a green **Signed in** + **Sign Out** (ចាកចេញពីគណនី), which clears the tokens and toasts `Signed out from SongSelect`. **Storage split (2026-08-24b)**: `clientId` / `redirectUri` / `accessTokenExpiresAt` / `isDevMock` sit in the plaintext `song-select-setting`, while **Client Secret, Subscription Key and both OAuth tokens live in `song-select-setting-secret`, encrypted by the OS** — grepping `setting.json` for a key you just typed must return NOTHING. Sign Out and a **Clear All Settings** both wipe the secure half too. The header button opens songselect.ccli.com in the OS browser. Cross-window note (AI-key precedent): consumers read the stored blob fresh per use, but this card's own status re-reads only in its own window — a change made elsewhere shows after a reload. **Dev builds only**: a **`(dev) Use Mock Data`** button sits beside Sign In — one click fills all fake credentials (`dev-mock-client` …), signs in (**Signed in (mock)**) and makes every SongSelect request serve a canned 13-song catalog with no network; Sign Out in mock mode resets the WHOLE card to empty, not just the tokens. The flag is ignored outside dev even if hand-written into storage (src: src/plugins/song-select/SettingOthersSongSelectComp.tsx · src/plugins/song-select/songSelectDevMockHelpers.ts · src/plugins/song-select/songSelectAuthHelpers.ts · electron/oauthHelpers.ts) |

## SC — `screen.html` (presentation output window) — **MANDATORY core: SC-01..02**

> **CDP facts (verified 2026-07-08):** while a screen is SHOWING it **is** a normal CDP
> target — `https://localhost:3000/screen.html?screenId=N` in `list_pages`, fully
> drivable (snapshot / click / screenshot). The target vanishes when the screen hides;
> a hidden screen's console forwards to the **electron main stdout** (the `npm run dev`
> terminal) via `all:app:log`. Never `navigate_page` the main window to `screen.html` —
> reach it only through SP-01 + `list_pages`. Screen-only bugs (e.g. full-width PDF) do
> NOT reproduce in the presenter's mini preview — that is why driving the real target is
> mandatory.

| ID    | Target                                                                                       | Interactions                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        | Pass condition                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| ----- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| SC-01 | Screen target attach                                                                         | present content → SP-01 show → `list_pages` → `select_page` → readiness → screenshot                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                | the `screen.html?screenId=N` target MUST appear and be drivable; screenshot captured from the screen target itself (not just the mini preview)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| SC-02 | Layer rendering on the real output                                                           | while bg + slide + bible + foreground are live                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      | all live layers composite correctly **on the screen target's own screenshot**, and the mini-screen mirrors it; compare the two for screen-only rendering bugs                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| SC-03 | ⌨️ `Ctrl/Alt+ArrowLeft/Right` on the screen target                                           | with a bible verse live, `press_key` on the selected screen page                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | bible verse steps prev/next on the output (mirror on mini-screen)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| SC-04 | `ScreenCloseButtonComp` (❌ `#close`)                                                        | 🖱️ on the screen target                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             | screen hides; its CDP target disappears; the presenter's `ShowHideScreen` reflects hidden                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| SC-05 | Hidden-screen log forwarding                                                                 | after hiding, trigger screen activity; read the `npm run dev` terminal                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              | screen console lines arrive via `all:app:log` on electron-main stdout (use this channel when hunting screen-only bugs while hidden)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| SC-06 | Output window invalid/missing `screenId` error state (`ScreenAppComp` null-manager branch)   | observe `screen.html` loaded with no / NaN `screenId`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               | `useScreenManager` returns null → a red "Screen ID is not provided in the URL…" panel on black renders and the `#close` button is force-shown (`opacity:1`), whose click calls `globalThis.close()` (no manager to hide); likely BLOCKED at runtime since it is reachable only via a stray target — never `navigate_page` the main window to `screen.html` (src: src/_screen/ScreenAppComp.tsx:16-32,64-95; src/_screen/ScreenCloseButtonComp.tsx:15-29)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| SC-07 | Output window auto-reload on resize (`screen.tsx` window `resize` listener)                  | resize the showing `screen.html` window (`resize_page`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             | The `window` `resize` event calls `appProvider.reload()`, so the screen target reloads (assets refetch, target briefly re-inits then reattaches in `list_pages`); drive only on a non-live display, else EX-02 (src: src/screen.tsx:40-42)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| SC-08 | **Lyric previewer↔screen render parity** (run on a COLD start, before any reload/re-present) | change **Extra Font Size** in the stage's ⚙ panel (PM-117) FIRST, then present a lyric slide, show the screen, and measure the same slide on both sides: `getComputedStyle` of `.ol-preview-line, .ol-preview-lyric-segment__text` inside `#slide` on the `screen.html` target vs. inside each presenter `ShadowingFillParentWidthComp` shadow root | `fontSize` and `color` MUST match. A screen showing open-lyric's raw `16px` default while the previewer shows the configured size (`DEFAULT_OPEN_LYRIC_FONT_SIZE + extraSlideFontSize`, e.g. 61px) is a **High** finding — lyric slide HTML is generated by the `open-lyric` dep and its options come from state that only the presenter's `LyricSlidesPreviewerComp` populates, so init-order bugs surface on the first present after launch and "heal" after a re-present. Since 2026-08-07g the size also comes from `lyric-stage-style-<stage>.extraFontSize`, which is deliberately UNPREFIXED — a screen that renders the default 61px while the previewer shows the configured size means the two sides resolved different setting keys. The mini preview does NOT reliably expose it (KB §13; src: src/lyric-list/LyricAppDocumentStageAbstract.ts, src/lyric-list/LyricSlidesPreviewerComp.tsx:32) |

## CM — Context-menu items (right-click actions)

Each distinct right-click menu ITEM as its own unit (triggers are in PL/PM/SP/GL rows). Destructive items = confirm→Cancel (EX-05) or act on a scratch item.

- Emoji: 🖱️ click · 🖱️🖱️ dblclick · 🖱️R right-click · ⇕ drag · ⌨️ key ·
  🎚️ slider · ⌨️✎ input · 🖐️ hover.
- **(family)** = one row consolidating the same item across sibling hosts.
- **[D]** = destructive item; pass = confirm dialog appears → **Cancel (EX-05)**,
  or act on a scratch item created for the purpose.
- Assert the open item set with
  `[...document.querySelectorAll('#app-context-menu-container .app-context-menu-item')].map(e=>e.textContent)`.

## LT — Locale & theme passes — **MANDATORY core: LT-01..02**

> **Why LT-02 is mandatory, not a spot-check.** `tran()`
> (src: src/lang/langHelpers.ts:601-625) short-circuits when the locale is `en-US`
> (`DEFAULT_LOCALE`) and returns the input string — **no dictionary lookup happens**. In
> `km-KH` the same call **throws** `Translation for text "…" not found in locale km-KH`
> when the key is absent, and there is no error boundary, so the component's whole
> subtree renders **blank**. An English-only run therefore cannot detect a missing
> translation _at all_, and `npm run lint` (tests + typecheck + build) stays green while
> a screen is broken in Khmer. Observed 2026-07-26: `PositionSizeFieldComp` called
> `tran(name)` with `name="X:"` and blanked the entire slide-editor tools panel.
>
> Two things hide from a source grep for `tran('literal')`, so only a live locale switch
> finds them: **concatenation** (`tran('a ' + 'b')` is ONE key at runtime) and **dynamic**
> `tran(prop)` fed by a JSX literal at the call site.

| ID    | Target                                          | Interactions                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | Pass condition                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| ----- | ----------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| LT-01 | Primary pass                                    | full matrix in the CURRENT locale/theme; record which locale that was (read it from Settings → Language's active button, NOT `localStorage`)                                                                                                    | (this is the main run); the starting locale is captured so LT-02 can restore it                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| LT-02 | **Secondary locale pass (MANDATORY)**           | switch via ST-04 → `Apply Settings` (reloads every window: re-`list_pages`/`select_page`, all `uid`s die); re-walk every screen the run touched + the presenter baseline; screenshot + `list_console_messages` each; then switch back and Apply | **no `Translation for text "…" not found in locale km-KH` in any console** (each occurrence = Critical finding: name the key AND the component from the React warning that follows); no blank/empty panel that rendered in the other locale; labels actually translate (KB §1 map), no raw i18n keys, no clipped/overflowing Khmer text; starting locale **restored** |
| LT-03 | Dark theme spot-check                           | via ST-05; screenshot presenter + settings                                                                                                                                                                                                      | readable contrast; no invisible text; **restore**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| LT-04 | Light theme spot-check                          | via ST-05                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       | same; **restore**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| LT-05 | `SettingGeneralThemeComp` "System" theme option | ⌨️✎ theme `<select>` → "System"; emulate OS `prefers-color-scheme`; **restore**                                                                                                                                                                 | app follows the OS scheme — `data-bs-theme`/documentElement resolves to OS light/dark and flips when the emulated OS scheme flips (distinct from LT-03 dark / LT-04 light); restore original theme (src: src/setting/SettingGeneralThemeComp.tsx:31-34)                                                                                                               |
