## MD — Media download from URL (mandatory core, needs network)

The only rows that exercise the external binaries. `downloadVideoOrAudio`
(`src/server/appHelpers.ts`) spawns `extra-bin/yt/yt-dlp`, pointing it at
`extra-bin/ffmpeg/bin` (`--ffmpeg-location`) and `extra-bin/qjs/qjs`
(`--no-js-runtimes --js-runtimes quickjs:<path>`).

**Those three are NOT in the app package.** They live in
`<data parent dir>/extra-bin/` (dev: `Desktop\open-worship-data-dev\extra-bin`) and
are installed on demand from **Settings → Others → Extra Binaries** — so `MD-05`
runs FIRST on any machine where the pack is absent, and `MD-06` is the guard that
makes the absence visible instead of a cryptic spawn failure. In dev the install
copies `extra-work/experiment-building/release/bin-<ver>.tar.gz`, which `npm i`
builds (the `install` lifecycle → `extra-work/build.sh`); nothing is downloaded.

Use the canonical link from the mandatory-core section above.

| ID    | Target                                           | Interactions                                                                 | Pass condition                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| ----- | ------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| MD-01 | Video download from URL (`BackgroundVideosComp`) | 🖱️R Videos tab empty area → `Download From URL` → ⌨️✎ link → `Ok`            | progress bar runs; the finished file appears in the videos dir AND as a new thumbnail in the tab (dir listing refreshes itself). yt-dlp merges video+audio via ffmpeg, so a merged container proves the shipped ffmpeg works (src: src/background/BackgroundVideosComp.tsx:160-201 · src/server/appHelpers.ts:219-323). **On FAILURE the toast now names the cause** — `Error occurred during downloading video: <reason>`, the reason being the LAST `ERROR:` line of the yt-dlp transcript with its `[extractor] <id>:` scope and the `Download failed:` wrapper stripped, capped at 200 chars (`toDownloadFailureReason`, src/background/downloadHelper.tsx). A bare sentence with no reason after it means the rejection carried nothing parseable, not that the reason was dropped. Untranslated on purpose: it is upstream tool output |
| MD-02 | Audio download from URL (`BackgroundAudiosComp`) | 🖱️R ♫Audios♫ split empty area → `Download From URL` → ⌨️✎ same link → `Ok`   | popup label reads **Audio URL:** (not Video URL); result is an **`.mp3`** in the audios dir — the app passes `-x --audio-format mp3 --audio-quality 0`, so this is the only row proving the shipped ffmpeg has an mp3 encoder (`libmp3lame`) (src: src/background/BackgroundAudiosComp.tsx:32-76)                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| MD-03 | Invalid-URL guard (`askForURL`)                  | ⌨️✎ a non-`http` string → `Ok`                                               | no download starts; toast "Invalid URL". Empty input marks the box `is-invalid` (src: src/background/downloadHelper.tsx:54-78)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| MD-04 | **Teardown — remove what MD-01/MD-02 wrote** [D] | 🖱️R the new video row → `Move to Trash` → `Yes`; same for the new `.mp3` row | each row leaves its tab immediately (no manual reload) and the file is gone from the videos/audios dir — it goes to the OS Recycle Bin via `shell.trashItem`, so it is recoverable, not shredded. End state: **no copy of the canonical title and no `temp-*.part` in either dir**. Doubles as CM-06 coverage on a background media row, against the one file the trash rule allows deleting — the scratch file this run created (src: src/others/FileItemHandlerComp.tsx:77 · src/background/BackgroundMediaItemComp.tsx:89) |
| MD-05 | **Extra Binaries panel** (`SettingOthersExtraBinComp`) — runs BEFORE MD-01 | ST tab `Others` → read the card; if `Not installed`, 🖱️ `Download and Install`; then 🖱️ `Re-extract` | the card names the `extra-bin` folder, an installed version and the latest available one (`Could not check for updates` is acceptable offline, and must NOT blank the installed half). After installing, `<data parent>\extra-bin` holds `yt/`, `ffmpeg/bin/`, `qjs/`, `info.json` **and the `bin-*.tar.gz` — the archive is kept on purpose**, so `Re-extract` succeeds with no network. When the published pack is newer the primary button reads `Update to <ver>` and, after it runs, the superseded `bin-*.tar.gz` is gone (src: src/setting/SettingOthersExtraBinComp.tsx · src/helper/extra-bin/extraBinInstallHelpers.ts) |
| MD-06 | **Missing-pack guard** (`requireExtraBinPaths`)   | rename/remove `<data parent>\extra-bin\yt`, then run MD-01's `Download From URL` | a confirm dialog **Media Tools Required** naming the missing binaries; `No` cancels with **no second "download failed" toast**; `Yes` opens Settings on the `Others` tab. **No yt-dlp process is spawned either way.** Restore the folder (or re-run MD-05) afterwards (src: src/helper/extra-bin/extraBinHelpers.ts · src/background/BackgroundVideosComp.tsx) |

**MD-04 in detail — the block owns its own garbage.** Each canonical download is ~100 MB
of video plus ~5 MB of mp3, and the app de-duplicates by suffixing rather than
overwriting, so an uncleaned block is not idempotent: it adds a fresh copy every run. On
2026-08-07 the dev data dir held **17 stale copies — ≈635 MB** — left
by earlier runs, and they had to be swept by hand; that is what this row exists to stop.

1. **Sweep first, download second.** Before MD-01, list the two dirs and delete any
   leftovers from earlier runs — they all carry the **canonical video's page title**
   (`[MV] គ្រប់ទាំងផ្កា Flowers by … - Official Music Video - YouTube`, with a ` (N)`
   suffix from the second copy on). Match that title, not `YouTube` (step 3). Report the
   count in the run's note — leftovers mean a previous run skipped MD-04.
2. **Prefer the app's own delete** (the row above): it proves CM-06, refreshes the list
   through the real `delete` event, and also trashes the material files
   (`trashAllMaterialFiles`). The **Move to Trash** entry is **hidden while the item is on
   a screen** (`isInScreen`, PM-35) — clear/hide the screen first or the menu looks broken.
3. **On-disk fallback** (item never appeared in the list, download failed halfway, or the
   app is already closed). Two traps: the names start with `[MV]`, and `[` is a
   character-class metacharacter for PowerShell's `-Path` (filter objects and pipe them,
   never glob); and **`*YouTube*` is far too broad a match** — the user's own library
   holds legitimately-downloaded files whose names end in `- YouTube` too (verified
   2026-08-07: `ស្រែកថ្វាយព្រះអង្គ Shout to the Lord - YouTube.MKV`, `4K Christian Church
Worship … - YouTube.mp4`). Match the **canonical video's title**:

   ```powershell
   $dirs = "$env:USERPROFILE\Desktop\open-worship-data-dev\videos",
           "$env:USERPROFILE\Desktop\open-worship-data-dev\audios"
   $dirs | ForEach-Object {
       Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath $_ |
           Where-Object { $_.Name -like '*Flowers by*Official Music Video - YouTube*' -or
                          $_.Name -like 'temp-*' } |
           Remove-Item   # binds PSPath → -LiteralPath, so the brackets are safe
   }
   ```

   List the matches before deleting anything, and prefer the Recycle Bin over
   `Remove-Item` when sweeping someone's data dir:
   `[Microsoft.VisualBasic.FileIO.FileSystem]::DeleteFile($p,'OnlyErrorDialogs','SendToRecycleBin')`
   (after `Add-Type -AssemblyName Microsoft.VisualBasic`).

   (Dev data lives in `…\Desktop\open-worship-data-dev`, NOT the non-`-dev` dir; if the
   folder settings were changed, read the actual path off the Background panel's
   folder-path bar.) A file deleted behind the app's back leaves a **stale thumbnail**
   until the tab is reloaded — expected, not a finding.

4. Deleting is **not** optional on failure: a run that reports MD-01/MD-02 BLOCKED still
   sweeps, because a partial download leaves the biggest debris.
5. The sweep covers the **downloaded media only**. `<data parent>\extra-bin` (~27 MB
   archive + ~36 MB extracted) is the installed tool pack, not this run's garbage — leave
   it. Deleting it just makes the next run re-install it, and MD-06 already proves the
   absent case by moving one folder aside temporarily.

**Reading a failure — do not report it as a code bug without this triage:**

0. **Is the pack installed at all?** Check `<data parent>\extra-bin` for
   `yt/yt-dlp.exe`, `ffmpeg/bin/ffmpeg.exe` and `qjs/qjs.exe`. Missing means MD-05 was
   skipped — the app should have shown the **Media Tools Required** dialog, and if it ran
   yt-dlp anyway that IS a bug (MD-06).
1. `ERROR: unable to download video data: HTTP Error 403: Forbidden` (often mid-transfer,
   after tens of MB) is **YouTube-side throttling**, not the app. It is likeliest when the
   same video was pulled minutes earlier. Retry once before filing anything.
2. Confirm which layer broke by running the binary directly — a 10 KB probe that does not
   touch the app:
   `extra-bin\yt\yt-dlp.exe --no-js-runtimes --js-runtimes quickjs:<qjs> --no-playlist --test -o <tmp>\p.%(ext)s <link>`
   (`--test` truncates to 10 KB; the trailing `Postprocessing: Conversion failed!` is
   expected from truncated input and is NOT a failure).
3. `WARNING: No supported JavaScript runtime could be found` = the qjs copy is missing or
   the flags regressed → real Critical finding. Verify with `-v`: the debug header must
   read `JS runtimes: quickjs-<version>` and the extractor line `[jsc:quickjs] Solving JS
challenges using quickjs`.
4. **Known app bug (pre-existing, do not re-file as new):** a failed download leaves its
   `temp-<ts>.f<fmt>.*.part` behind in the data dir — the error path only checks for the
   final file. MD-04 removes it; note that it had to.
5. A download that succeeds when the destination name already exists lands as
   `<name> (1).<ext>` — expected de-duplication, not a bug. But seeing `(1)` at all on the
   **first** download of a run means MD-04 was skipped last time (step 1 above).

BLOCKED is acceptable **only** with no network; say so in `note`. Never mark MD PASS from
a toast alone — check the file on disk (or the refreshed thumbnail), per the evidence
rule. MD-04 is never BLOCKED by "no network": with nothing downloaded it is the sweep
alone, and it still runs.

GL 23 · NAV 21 · PL 102 · PM 127 · PR 29 · RD 79 · ED 46 · ST 51 · PU 20 · SP 22 ·
SC 8 · XW 10 · EX 7 · CM 96 · KB 60 · LT 5 · MD 6 · AP 8 = **720 rows total**. Compute the
denominator per run as `720 − EXCLUDED` (hardware and policy exclusions vary by machine).

> whole **AP** block (8 rows) was missing from the sum until 2026-08-07f, and it was
> 15 rows behind again (651 vs 666) until 2026-08-08i — and 7 behind (678 vs 685, the
> whole RD-65..RD-71 tail) until 2026-08-09.
> Re-run that count whenever you add
> rows. **PL is no longer dev-gated**: none of PL-10 / PL-29 / PL-32..PL-99 may be
> excluded as "dev-only" (PL-49).

> Reminder: whatever the focus area, the **mandatory core** — screen (SP-01, SP-02,
> SC-01, SC-02, PR-04, one clear key), **locale (LT-01, LT-02)** and **media download
> (MD-01, MD-02) plus its teardown (MD-04)** — must appear in every run's state file.
